title: Republic of Uzbekistan
capsule: Uzbekistan declared independence from the Soviet Union on 1 September 1991 and was recognized internationally following the USSR's formal dissolution in December 1991, making the Wikidata from date of 1992 reflect the period of full international recognition. Under Islam Karimov, who had governed as Communist Party first secretary since 1989 and served as president until his death in 2016, the state maintained authoritarian single-party rule, a slow transition from Soviet command economy, and a foreign policy of regional centrality contested with Russia and China. The country encompasses the ancient Silk Road cities of Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva, and holds the second largest cotton industry in the former Soviet space. Shavkat Mirziyoyev succeeded Karimov in 2016 and pursued selective political and economic opening.
